title: Explicit coefficient pushout of a square-zero algebra extension
statement:
Let $R$ and $B$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure on $B$. Let $K,N$ be $B$-modules and let $0\to K\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{p}B\to0$ be an exact sequence of additive groups in which $E$ is a commutative $R$-algebra, $p$ is an $R$-algebra map, $j(K)$ is a square-zero ideal, and $e\,j(k)=j(p(e)k)$ for $e\in E$, $k\in K$. For any $B$-linear map $v:K\to N$, give $T=E\oplus N$ the trivial square-zero multiplication of [def-sc-trivial-square-zero-extension], with $E$ acting on $N$ through $p$. The additive subgroup
$$J_v=\{(j(k),-v(k)):k\in K\}\subset T$$
is an ideal. Put $E_v=T/J_v$, $j_v(n)=[(0,n)]$, $p_v([(e,n)])=p(e)$, and $q_v(e)=[(e,0)]$. These maps are well-defined, $E_v$ is a commutative $R$-algebra, $q_v,p_v$ are $R$-algebra maps, and
$$0\to N\xrightarrow{j_v}E_v\xrightarrow{p_v}B\to0$$
is exact with square-zero kernel and its prescribed $B$-action. Moreover $q_vj=j_vv$.
For any $B$-module $L$, any such square-zero $R$-algebra extension $0\to L\xrightarrow{j_D}D\xrightarrow{p_D}B\to0$, any $B$-linear map $w:N\to L$, and any $R$-algebra map $h:E\to D$ with $p_Dh=p$ and $hj=j_Dwv$, there is a unique $R$-algebra map $\bar h:E_v\to D$ satisfying $\bar hq_v=h$ and $\bar hj_v=j_Dw$. It is given by $\bar h([(e,n)])=h(e)+j_D(w(n))$ and satisfies $p_D\bar h=p_v$. This is the coefficient pushout of the extension along $v$. No flatness or finiteness hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Restrict the $B$-module structure on $N$ along $p:E\to B$. By [def-sc-trivial-square-zero-extension], $T$ has multiplication $(e,n)(e',n')=(ee',p(e)n'+p(e')n)$, unit $(1,0)$ and componentwise addition. Its $R$-structure is $r\mapsto(\iota_E(r),0)$. This agrees with the restricted action since $p$ is an $R$-algebra map.

source.place: Tag 0GPW, remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial, first displayed diagram and the sentence defining (N times B prime)/M with antidiagonal M; explicit ring law and universal property of this coefficient-pushout construction.

proof.text:
The map $k\mapsto(j(k),-v(k))$ is additive, so its image $J_v$ is an additive subgroup. For $e\in E,n\in N,k\in K$, the multiplication formula gives
$$(e,n)(j(k),-v(k))=(e j(k),-p(e)v(k)+p(j(k))n)=(j(p(e)k),-v(p(e)k)).$$
Here $p j=0$, the prescribed action gives the first coordinate, and $B$-linearity of $v$ gives the second. Thus $J_v$ is closed under multiplication by arbitrary elements of $T$ and is an ideal.

source.place: Tag 0GPW, remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial, first displayed diagram and the sentence defining (N times B prime)/M with antidiagonal M; explicit ring law and universal property of this coefficient-pushout construction.

proof.text: Apply [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] to $T,J_v$: $E_v=T/J_v$ is a commutative $R$-algebra with surjective quotient map. Representatives $(e,n),(e',n')$ give the same class exactly when $(e-e',n-n')=(j(k),-v(k))$ for some $k$. Hence $p(e)=p(e')$, so $p_v$ is well-defined. The formula for multiplication shows $p_v$ preserves products and the unit; addition and the $R$-structure are immediate. The inclusion $e\mapsto(e,0)$ also preserves all these operations, hence so does $q_v$. The map $j_v$ is additive.

source.place: Tag 0GPW, remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial, first displayed diagram and the sentence defining (N times B prime)/M with antidiagonal M; explicit ring law and universal property of this coefficient-pushout construction.

proof.text: If $j_v(n)=0$, then $(0,n)=(j(k),-v(k))$ for some $k$. Injectivity of $j$ gives $k=0$, hence $n=0$. Surjectivity of $p$ gives surjectivity of $p_v$. If $p_v([(e,n)])=0$, exactness of the original extension gives $e=j(k)$ for some $k$, and the defining relation yields $[(e,n)]=[(0,n+v(k))]=j_v(n+v(k))$. Conversely $p_v j_v=0$. This proves exactness. Also $(j(k),-v(k))\in J_v$ gives $q_v j(k)=j_v v(k)$.

source.place: Tag 0GPW, remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial, first displayed diagram and the sentence defining (N times B prime)/M with antidiagonal M; explicit ring law and universal property of this coefficient-pushout construction.

proof.text: The multiplication formula gives $(0,n)(0,n')=(0,0)$ and $(e,m)(0,n)=(0,p(e)n)$. Passing to classes proves that the kernel $j_v(N)$ has square zero and that $xj_v(n)=j_v(p_v(x)n)$ for every $x\in E_v$. Thus its induced $B$-module action is the prescribed one, independently of the lift of an element of $B$.

source.place: Tag 0GPW, remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial, first displayed diagram and the sentence defining (N times B prime)/M with antidiagonal M; explicit ring law and universal property of this coefficient-pushout construction.

proof.text:
For the given $D,w,h$, set $F(e,n)=h(e)+j_D(w(n))$. This is additive, sends $(1,0)$ to $1$, and sends $(\iota_E(r),0)$ to $\iota_D(r)$. Using the prescribed action in $D$, $p_Dh=p$, $B$-linearity of $w$, and $j_D(L)^2=0$, expand to obtain
$$F(e,n)F(e',n')=h(ee')+j_D(p(e)w(n')+p(e')w(n))=F(ee',p(e)n'+p(e')n).$$
So $F:T\to D$ is an $R$-algebra map. Moreover $F(j(k),-v(k))=hj(k)-j_Dwv(k)=0$, so it kills $J_v$.

source.place: Tag 0GPW, remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial, first displayed diagram and the sentence defining (N times B prime)/M with antidiagonal M; explicit ring law and universal property of this coefficient-pushout construction.

proof.text: If two representatives differ by $(j(k),-v(k))$, their $F$-values differ by zero by the preceding calculation. Thus $\bar h([(e,n)])=F(e,n)$ is well-defined. Since addition, multiplication and the $R$-structure on the quotient are induced on representatives, the corresponding identities for $F$ prove that $\bar h$ is an $R$-algebra map. Substitution of $(e,0)$ and $(0,n)$ gives $\bar hq_v=h$ and $\bar hj_v=j_Dw$. Also $p_D\bar h([(e,n)])=p(e)$ since $p_Dj_D=0$, proving $p_D\bar h=p_v$.

source.place: Tag 0GPW, remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial, first displayed diagram and the sentence defining (N times B prime)/M with antidiagonal M; explicit ring law and universal property of this coefficient-pushout construction.

proof.text: Every class decomposes as $[(e,n)]=q_v(e)+j_v(n)$. Any $R$-algebra map with the two required restrictions must therefore send it to $h(e)+j_Dw(n)$, proving uniqueness. This is precisely the coefficient-pushout universal property asserted in the statement. Each construction and calculation used only the stated exactness, module actions and square-zero identities; no flatness, finiteness, splitting, or injectivity of $v$ was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q102-9fc8c3dda (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks defos.tex Tag 0GPW (remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial, line 309 onward). The item states the source's B'_1=(N×B')/M with M embedded antidiagonally. It correctly reads that product as the trivial square-zero extension E⊕N, with E acting on N through p. It also states the pushout's universal property, with w arbitrary. No new nodes, no tool_uses, and no repair note, so this is not a 2026-10-21 re-split. The two cited nodes are definitions. def-sc-trivial-square-zero-extension gives the product (r,m)(s,t)=(rs,rt+sm). def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient gives the quotient algebra, its surjective quotient map and its kernel J. I recomputed every step. Step 2: J_v is an ideal, using pj=0, e j(k)=j(p(e)k) and B-linearity of v. Step 4: j_v is injective because j is (v need not be), and ker p_v=im j_v via [(j(k),n)]=[(0,n+v(k))]. Step 5: the kernel has square zero and carries the prescribed B-action. Step 6: F is multiplicative, using p_D h=p, the action in D and j_D(L)^2=0, and F kills J_v because hj=j_D w v. Steps 7-8: the induced map descends, satisfies p_D h̄=p_v, and is unique by additivity. All steps are genuinely elementary. Edge cases checked: v=0 gives B⊕N; N=0 gives B; K=0 gives B⊕N; v=id gives E; the nonsplit Z/4→F_2 case returns Z/4; characteristic 2 needs no sign exception. Duplicate search (rg -L for antidiagonal, 0GPW, and square-zero with pushout) found nothing equivalent; lem-sfb-affine-commutative-extension-pushout is about group schemes. The only citer, lem-per-conormal-extension-class-cokernel steps 4/5/7/8, uses exactly q_v j=j_v v, the universal property with w=id, and p_D h̄=p_v, all stated. The item cites only definitions, so there is no cycle. The statement is unchanged; the added stmt_dep def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient is genuinely used.
